title: Risk Assessment and Probability Estimation for Dilution Testing in Microbiology
text: food safety microbiology, accurate risk assessment crucial ensuring public health. Microbiological testing often involves dilution procedures quantify microbial contamination. dilutionrisk package addresses statistical challenges : Estimating true microbial concentration diluted samples Assessing detection probabilities different contamination levels Designing optimal sampling plans quality control Comparing dilution schemes cost-effective testing Validating theoretical models simulation studies

title: Coefficient of Variation for Heterogeneous Batches — cv_heterogeneous
text: mu Mean microbial count log scale. Must satisfy log() - log(f*u) <= mu <= log(b) - log(f*u). sd Standard deviation normal distribution log scale. Must positive. Lower bound cell count domain. Must non-negative. b Upper bound cell count domain. Must greater . f Final dilution factor. Must 0 1. u Amount placed plate. Must positive. USL Upper specification limit microbial count. n_sim Number simulations. Larger values provide precise estimates. Recommended minimum: 10,000.

title: Coefficient of Variation for Heterogeneous Batches — cv_heterogeneous
text: Numeric value representing coefficient variation heterogeneous batch.

title: Coefficient of Variation for Heterogeneous Batches — cv_heterogeneous
text: coefficient variation defined : $$CV = \frac{\sigma}{\mu}$$ \(\sigma\) standard deviation \(\mu\) mean estimated microbial concentration. heterogeneous batches, microbial count follows truncated Poisson-lognormal distribution, accounting variability contamination levels across batch.

what: dilutionrisk: Risk Assessment for Dilution Testing — dilutionrisk
title: dilutionrisk: Risk Assessment for Dilution Testing — dilutionrisk
text: dilutionrisk package implements statistical methods microbiological risk assessment food safety, focusing : Probability Detection (PD): Probability estimated microbial count exceeds upper specification limit. Probability Acceptance (PA): Probability batch accepted based sampling plans. Operating Characteristic (OC) Curves: Visual comparison different dilution schemes. Coefficient Variation (CV): Variability estimation different dilution schemes. True Concentration Estimation: Estimating true microbial concentration original sample.

title: dilutionrisk: Risk Assessment for Dilution Testing — dilutionrisk
text: Provides probability estimations graphical displays modelling assessment risk based aerobic plate count (APC) diluted testing. package supports two scenarios: Homogeneous Batches: Assumes microbial distribution uniform throughout batch. count follows truncated Poisson distribution. Heterogeneous Batches: Assumes microbial distribution non-uniform. count follows truncated Poisson-lognormal distribution. scenarios incorporate dilution factors plate amounts model dilution process microbiological testing.

title: Probability of Acceptance for Heterogeneous Batches — prob_acceptance_heterogeneous
text: probability acceptance calculated using binomial distribution: $$P_a = P(X \le c) = \sum_{k=0}^{c} \binom{n}{k} p_d^k (1-p_d)^{n-k}$$ \(p_d\) probability detection \(n\) number samples inspected.

title: Probability of Detection for Heterogeneous Batches — prob_detection_heterogeneous
text: probability detection defined probability estimated microbial count exceeds upper specification limit (USL). heterogeneous batches, count follows truncated Poisson-lognormal distribution. theoretical probability calculated integrating lognormal mixing distribution: $$P_d = 1 - \sum_{=1}^{USL \times f \times u} \frac{1}{!\sqrt{2\pi}\sigma}       \int_0^\infty \frac{t^{-1} \exp(-0.5((\log(t)-\mu_d)/\sigma)^2)}{e^t - 1} dt$$

title: Truncated Poisson Random Number Generation — rtpois
text: truncated Poisson distribution probability mass function: $$P(X = x) = \frac{\lambda^x e^{-\lambda}}{x! \sum_{k=}^{b} \frac{\lambda^k e^{-\lambda}}{k!}}$$ \(\le x \le b\). function uses rejection sampling maximum 1,000,000 iterations ensure convergence. lambda = 0, observations 0 within bounds.

title: Truncated Poisson Random Number Generation — rtpois
text: Johnson, N. L., Kemp, . W., & Kotz, S. (2005). Univariate Discrete Distributions (3rd ed.). Wiley.

title: Truncated Poisson Random Number Generation — rtpois
code:
# Generate 10 observations from truncated Poisson with lambda = 5 # bounded between 0 and 300 set.seed(123) rtpois(n = 10, lambda = 5, a = 0, b = 300) #>  [1] 4 7 4 8 9 2 5 8 5 5  # Generate 5 observations with lower bound 10 and upper bound 50 rtpois(n = 5, lambda = 20, a = 10, b = 50) #> [1] 27 22 14 12 25  # Lambda = 0 case (all zeros) rtpois(n = 5, lambda = 0, a = 0, b = 300) #> [1] 0 0 0 0 0  # Generate for different lambda values lambdas <- c(1, 5, 10, 20) set.seed(456) for (lam in lambdas) {   cat("Lambda =", lam, ":",       rtpois(n = 3, lambda = lam, a = 0, b = 100), "
") } #> Lambda = 1 : 0 0 1  #> Lambda = 5 : 7 7 4  #> Lambda = 10 : 5 9 7  #> Lambda = 20 : 21 24 22   # Compare with regular Poisson (when bounds are wide) set.seed(789) trunc_sample <- rtpois(n = 1000, lambda = 10, a = 0, b = 300) regular_sample <- rpois(n = 1000, lambda = 10)  # Both should be similar when bounds are not restrictive cat("Truncated mean:", mean(trunc_sample), "
") #> Truncated mean: 9.963  cat("Regular mean:", mean(regular_sample), "
") #> Regular mean: 9.927   # When bounds are restrictive (0-10 only) set.seed(321) trunc_restricted <- rtpois(n = 1000, lambda = 20, a = 0, b = 10) cat("Restricted truncated mean:", mean(trunc_restricted), "
") #> Restricted truncated mean: 9.253   # Note: Rejection sampling may be slow for very restrictive bounds # or very large lambda values

title: Truncated Poisson-Lognormal Random Number Generation — rtrunpoilog
text: vector random numbers truncated Poisson-lognormal distribution. Returns NA rejection sampling fails converge. vector random numbers truncated Poisson-lognormal distribution.

title: Truncated Poisson-Lognormal Random Number Generation — rtrunpoilog
text: Poisson-lognormal distribution mixture distribution : \(\Lambda \sim \text{Lognormal}(\mu, \sigma^2)\) \(X | \Lambda = \lambda \sim \text{Poisson}(\lambda)\) truncation limits support \(\le X \le b\). probability mass function given : $$P(X = x) = \frac{1}{x! \sqrt{2\pi}\sigma}       \int_0^\infty \lambda^{x-1} e^{-\lambda}       \exp\left(-\frac{(\log(\lambda)-\mu)^2}{2\sigma^2}\right) d\lambda$$ distribution particularly useful modeling microbial counts heterogeneous (non-homogeneous) batches contamination level varies across batch. Poisson-lognormal distribution mixture distribution : \(\Lambda \sim \text{Lognormal}(\mu, \sigma^2)\) \(X | \Lambda = \lambda \sim \text{Poisson}(\lambda)\) truncation limits support \(\le X \le b\).

title: Truncated Poisson-Lognormal Random Number Generation — rtrunpoilog
text: Gonzales-Barron, U.., Pilão Cadavez, V.., Butler, F., 2013. Statistical approaches design sampling plans microbiological monitoring foods. : Mathematical Statistical Methods Food Science Technology. Wiley, pp. 363–384. Bulmer, M. G. (1974). fitting Poisson lognormal distribution species-abundance data. Biometrics, 30(1), 101-110.

title: Truncated Poisson-Lognormal Random Number Generation — rtrunpoilog
code:
# Generate 10 observations from truncated Poisson-lognormal # with mu = 2, sd = 0.5, bounded between 0 and 300 set.seed(123) rtrunpoilog(n = 10, mu = 2, sd = 0.5, a = 0, b = 300) #>  [1]  9  8 17  9  9 17  7  2 10  9  # Generate with different parameters set.seed(456) rtrunpoilog(n = 5, mu = 1, sd = 0.3, a = 0, b = 100) #> [1] 1 2 5 3 2  # Compare with regular Poisson-lognormal (when bounds are wide) set.seed(789) n_sim <- 1000 trunc_sample <- rtrunpoilog(n = n_sim, mu = 2, sd = 0.5, a = 0, b = 300) regular_sample <- rpois(n = n_sim, lambda = rlnorm(n_sim, 2, 0.5))  cat("Truncated mean:", mean(trunc_sample), "
") #> Truncated mean: 8.363  cat("Regular mean:", mean(regular_sample), "
") #> Regular mean: 8.599  cat("Truncated variance:", var(trunc_sample), "
") #> Truncated variance: 27.75298  cat("Regular variance:", var(regular_sample), "
") #> Regular variance: 27.72592   # When bounds are restrictive (0-10 only) set.seed(321) trunc_restricted <- rtrunpoilog(n = n_sim, mu = 3, sd = 0.8, a = 0, b = 10) #> Error: The truncated Poisson lognormal (TPLN) random variable must be bounded by a and b, #> which means that mu must be between log(a) and log(b). #> Current mu = 3.0000, bounds: [-Inf, 2.3026] cat("Restricted truncated mean:", mean(trunc_restricted), "
") #> Error: object 'trunc_restricted' not found  # Generate samples with different sd values mu_val <- 2 sd_values <- c(0.2, 0.5, 1.0) set.seed(654) for (sd_val in sd_values) {   sample <- rtrunpoilog(n = 10, mu = mu_val, sd = sd_val, a = 0, b = 300)   cat("mu =", mu_val, "sd =", sd_val, ":",       summary(sample), "
") } #> mu = 2 sd = 0.2 : 4 6 6 7.1 7.75 13  #> mu = 2 sd = 0.5 : 3 6.25 7.5 7.4 8.75 12  #> mu = 2 sd = 1 : 1 2.25 9 12.8 16.25 36   # Note: Rejection sampling may be slow for very restrictive bounds # or when sd is very large  # Generate 100 random values set.seed(123) rtrunpoilog(n = 100, mu = 0, sd = 1, a = 0, b = 300) #>   [1]  0  3  5  1  1  8  1  0  0  0  3  1  0  1  0  7  1  0  3  2  0  3  1  1  0 #>  [26]  0  2  1  0  6  2  0  2  0  1  1  1  2  0  1  0  1  0 10  2  1  0  2  5  1 #>  [51]  0  0  1  3  1  6  0  1  1  2  3  2  1  2  0  1  1  0  0  8  1  0  1  0  1 #>  [76]  4  3  0  0  1  2  0  0  1  0  1  1  1  0  4  2  0  0  1  5  1 16  2  0  1  # Generate a single value rtrunpoilog(n = 1, mu = 0.5, sd = 0.8, a = 10, b = 200) #> Error: The truncated Poisson lognormal (TPLN) random variable must be bounded by a and b, #> which means that mu must be between log(a) and log(b). #> Current mu = 0.5000, bounds: [2.3026, 5.2983]
